_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics (Standard) 041, Term-II 2022, Series PPQQB/3 SET-1. 11 pages: idx 0 bilingual cover (Maximum Marks 40, 14 questions, 11 printed pages), idx 1 Hindi instructions + Q1-3, idx 2 English instructions + Q1-3; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-10, Hindi on every odd index 1-9 (each odd page is the Hindi of the page after it). Every odd page was checked at full size or on the contact sheet and opens in Hindi (idx 7 is wholly Hindi: Q11(b), Q12, Q13); the last page, idx 10, is English (Case Study 2, Q14). No parity inversion, no English spill onto an odd page. Q11(a) ends idx 6 with its OR and Q11(b) opens idx 8. Printed structure (instructions iii-v): A Q1-6 x2, B Q7-10 x3, C Q11-14 x4 with two case study based questions (Q13 'Case Study - 1', Q14 'Case Study - 2', each two parts (a)/(b) of 2 marks); 12 + 12 + 16 = 40. Matches term2_m10 exactly. Internal choice is counted by the instructions: two in A, one in B, one in C = 4, and the marking scheme reprints both branches of exactly Q1, Q4, Q7 and Q11 (no OR in either case study). No MCQs, so every row is subjective with no key. Decimal points on this paper are RAISED (Q4(a) 1{\cdot}4, Q14(b) 0{\cdot}5 and 1{\cdot}5). Q7(a) and Q7(b) are Constructions, filed on 'Constructions [Outdated]' under subtopic names taken from the pre-2023 NCERT Ch.11 sections (Division of a Line Segment; Construction of Tangents to a Circle), which no list declares yet. plan.txt: no reference papers, nothing skipped.

questions.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
questions.stem:
Solve the quadratic equation for x :
\(x^2 - 2ax - (4b^2 - a^2) = 0\)

questions.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
questions.stem:
If the quadratic equation
\((1 + a^2)x^2 + 2abx + (b^2 - c^2) = 0\)
has equal and real roots, then prove that :
\(b^2 = c^2(1 + a^2)\)

questions.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
questions.stem: Find the sum of first 20 terms of an AP in which \(d = 5\) and \(a_{20} = 135\).

questions.subtopic: Mode of Grouped Data
questions.stem:
Find the mode of the given frequency distribution :

| *Class* | *Frequency* |
|---|---|
| 15 – 25 | 6 |
| 25 – 35 | 11 |
| 35 – 45 | 22 |
| 45 – 55 | 23 |
| 55 – 65 | 14 |
| 65 – 75 | 5 |

questions.subtopic: Angle of Elevation Problems
questions.stem: The tops of two poles of heights 20 m and 28 m are connected with a wire. The wire is inclined to the horizontal at an angle of \(30^\circ\). Find the length of the wire and the distance between the two poles.

questions.subtopic: Mean of Grouped Data
questions.stem:
The weights (in kg) of 50 wild animals of a National Park were recorded and the following data was obtained :

| *Weight (in kg)* | *Number of animals* |
|---|---|
| 100 – 110 | 4 |
| 110 – 120 | 12 |
| 120 – 130 | 23 |
| 130 – 140 | 8 |
| 140 – 150 | 3 |

Find the mean weight (in kg) of animals, using assumed mean method.

questions.subtopic: Median of Grouped Data
questions.stem:
For the following frequency distribution, find the median :

| *Class* | *Frequency* |
|---|---|
| 1400 – 1550 | 6 |
| 1550 – 1700 | 13 |
| 1700 – 1850 | 25 |
| 1850 – 2000 | 10 |

questions.subtopic: Angle of Depression Problems
questions.stem: A straight highway leads to the foot of a tower. A man standing at the top of the tower observes a car at an angle of depression of \(30^\circ\), which is approaching the foot of the tower with a uniform speed. Ten seconds later, the angle of depression of the car is found to be \(60^\circ\). Find the time taken by the car to reach the foot of the tower from this point.

questions.context:
John planned a birthday party for his younger sister with his friends. They decided to make some birthday caps by themselves and to buy a cake from a bakery shop. For these two items, they decided the following dimensions :
Cake : Cylindrical shape with diameter 24 cm and height 14 cm.
Cap : Conical shape with base circumference 44 cm and height 24 cm.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: How many square cm paper would be used to make 4 such caps ?
